core_obligations: One direction (proof lines 10668-10678): vanishing of the cohomology of Z/l over the extension L in degree n is used, together with the prime-to-l transfer of the square root and the reduction to finite coefficient pieces, to deduce the vanishing of all l-torsion cohomology in degrees at least n over K.

The other direction (proof lines 10678-10691): conversely, the vanishing over K of the cohomology of l-torsion sheaves in degrees at least n gives, by the same reduction to the maximal pro-l extension, the vanishing of the cohomology of Z/l over L in degree n.
proof_roadmap: Translate both conditions into Galois cohomology of the pro-l subgroup.
Reduce arbitrary l-torsion coefficients to finite pieces.
Conclude the equivalence in both directions.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the higher-degree form of the reduction to the maximal pro-l extension: vanishing of the etale cohomology of all l-torsion sheaves over K in degrees at least n is equivalent to the single vanishing of the cohomology of Z/l over the field L fixed by a maximal pro-l subgroup (statement lines 10657-10666). The proof carries out the two directions by translating into Galois cohomology, reducing arbitrary l-torsion coefficients to finite pieces and using the pro-l property of the subgroup (proof lines 10668-10691). The non-formal content is the same reduction as in the degree-n case, now applied in all degrees. The claim is H2: two reductions, both written out.
